content.text:
The Child Who Just Loves Zooming Along

When a new kickboard or bicycle arrives, a child falls deep into the joy of speed. Shouting "Faster, faster!", they toss off the helmet as stuffy and race along without even looking ahead.

For a parent, the heart-stopping moments are more than one or two. But "No!" alone doesn't really change a child's mind. The child has to feel for themselves that 'riding safely is more fun.'

Curious about the kickboard safety story? We look at the lesson of the kickboard safety story through pictures. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read the kickboard safety story together with your child and talk it over. We've gathered all kinds of stories about "21. Slow Down, Look Ahead!"—helmet education stories, toddler safety stories, how to ride a kickboard, and more.

content.alt: 21. Slow Down, Look Ahead! - Why does the habit matter for kickboard safety?
content.text:
Why Does the Habit Matter for Kickboard Safety?

Most kickboard accidents start with 'speed' and 'not looking ahead.' One little pebble or one person suddenly passing by, and it's easy to lose your balance.

That's why safety should be built into an everyday habit rather than delivered as a warning in the moment. Wearing a helmet, slowing down, looking ahead—once these three become natural habits, a child can enjoy outdoor play far more safely.

content.alt: 21. Slow Down, Look Ahead! - What Hori taught Toto
content.text:
What Hori Taught Toto

In the story Slow Down, Look Ahead!, Toto rides without a helmet and nearly trips over a pebble. Hori, who comes rushing over, doesn't scold Toto.

Instead, Hori puts a blue helmet on him and says, "It's a sturdy hat that protects your head." Click—once the chin strap is snugly fastened, Toto smiles too and says, "Oh, this feels solid!" It's a scene that turns safety from something forced into something reassuring.

content.alt: 21. Slow Down, Look Ahead! - 3 safety promises from Tangobook
content.text:
3 Safety Promises From Tangobook

The heart of this story is three promises that are easy for a child to memorize. One, always wear a helmet when you ride! Two, not too fast—go slowly! Three, look ahead carefully, and if it's dangerous, stop with your foot!

Tangobook's story repeats these promises like a refrain, helping your child recall them naturally every time they ride a kickboard. Just like the scene where Toto stops with his foot when he sees the puppy Dubu, your child learns 'stopping' as play.

content.alt: 21. Slow Down, Look Ahead! - Safety play to try together at home
content.text:
Safety Play to Try Together at Home

After reading the book, turn putting on the helmet into a fun ritual. If your child picks their own helmet and fastens it with a "Click!", making it feel like play, they'll stop refusing the helmet.

Also, in the yard or a safe spot, practice slowing down and stopping with the foot on the signals "Slow!" and "Stop!" When you praise looking ahead well and stopping—specifically, rather than riding fast—your child feels proud of safe behavior.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How do I teach kickboard safety?

A. Set the promise together to go slowly and look ahead, and put a helmet on them. Learning how to ride safely joyfully through a kickboard safety story helps them take care on their own.

Q. My child wants to ride the kickboard too fast.

A. Tell them that riding safely, not fast, is what's cool. Praising them when they ride slowly and look ahead well helps a careful habit grow.

Q. What must we bring when riding a kickboard?

A. It's best to wear a helmet and pads and ride in a safe spot with few people. Practice stopping when you need to stop, together, like play.
